neighbours.label: Fires on the letter piece ' X' (and the piece right after it) at the start of a transliterated foreign name split into several tokens (Xhosa, Xerxes, Xuanzang, Xochimilco); quiet on foreign names that start with other letters.
fire: The museum holds beadwork made by Xhosa artisans in the Eastern Cape.
Historians still debate why Xerxes burned the temples of Athens.
The travelers stopped in Xalapa before heading to the coast.
The journals of Xuanzang describe the monasteries of central Asia.
Boats painted in bright colors carry families through Xochimilco.
The striker Xhaka signed a new contract with the club.
The ruins of Xanadu sit on the grasslands of Inner Mongolia.
The factory moved its main plant to Xiamen in the nineties.
quiet: The museum holds beadwork made by Tswana artisans in the Northern Cape.
Historians still debate why Pericles rebuilt the temples of Athens.
The travelers stopped in Puebla before heading to the coast.
The journals of Marco Polo describe the cities of central Asia.
Boats painted in bright colors carry families through Tlacotalpan.
The striker Kane signed a new contract with the club.
The ruins of Karakorum sit on the grasslands of Mongolia.

predictions: 6/8 fire >= 0.3 (probes 0.33-0.85); near misses mostly < 0.1, but Zanzibar scored 0.28, so one Z/Q-initial name near miss may leak; this test avoids Z names.
notes: Probes (fraction of max 16.6): Xhosa 0.85, Xochimilco 0.48, Xanadu 0.41, Xerxes 0.39, 'X hour' 0.35, Xuanzang 0.33; Zanzibar 0.28, Kilimanjaro 0.01. Fire names were checked to split as ' X' + pieces; near misses use similarly split names starting with K, T, M, B, P.
